title: A compact generative language model learns the compositional grammar of phase-separating proteins.
authors: Wasim, Abdul; Pramanik, Ushasi; Das, Anirban; Latua, Pikaso; Rudra, Jai S; Mondal, Jagannath
one_liner_zh: 该文用紧凑生成式语言模型从少量相分离蛋白序列学习无序蛋白的组成语法，生成序列并经粗粒化模拟与实验验证其凝聚体形成倾向，直接涉及IDP/相分离对象、序列-互作机制建模及AI方法，高度契合本课题。
abstract: Liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) of intrinsically disordered proteins drives the formation of biomolecular condensates, yet the sequence-level grammar that promotes condensation remains difficult to specify from first principles. Existing protein language models are typically trained on large, folded-protein-rich sequence corpora and may not optimally capture the compositional biases of LLPS-prone disordered proteins. Here, we show that a compact generative language model, with an architecture and size ( approximately 17 M parameters) selected via systematic hyperparameter optimization and cross-validation, trained from scratch on a small set of phase-separating protein sequences, can learn sequence features associated with condensate formation. The model generates thousands of sequences that reproduce length-dependent trends in disorder, charge decoration, hydropathy patterning, and sequence entropy, with training and generative behavior stable across independent seeds. Homology analysis indicates that generated sequences are not full-length copies of known proteins, but instead combine short segments matching natural proteins with a novel, model-generated sequence. Descriptor-based screening of short generated sequences yielded a pool of disordered candidates, from which five synthetically feasible peptides were selected for experimental testing. Four of them show condensate-like signatures under near-physiological conditions, including droplet-like assemblies and increased turbidity. Coarse-grained phase-coexistence simulations of a subset of generated sequences with longer lengths show a broad range of phase-separation tendencies, with 12 of 89 sequences comparable to the strongly phase-separating hnRNPA1 low-complexity domain. These results suggest that compact, task-specific generative models can learn information-rich sequence grammars from small curated datasets and propose experimentally testable condensate-forming peptides.
abstract_zh: intrinsically disordered proteins（本质无序蛋白）的液-液相分离（LLPS）驱动生物分子凝聚体的形成，然而促进凝聚的序列级语法仍难以从第一性原理加以明确。现有的蛋白质语言模型通常在大规模、富含折叠蛋白的序列语料上训练，可能无法最优地捕捉易发生LLPS的无序蛋白的组成偏差。在此，我们展示了一个紧凑的生成式语言模型，其架构和规模（约1700万参数）通过系统超参数优化和交叉验证选定，并在小型相分离蛋白序列集上从头训练，能够学习与凝聚体形成相关的序列特征。该模型生成数千条序列，再现了无序性、电荷装饰、疏水性模式及序列熵中的长度依赖性趋势，且训练和生成行为在不同独立种子下保持稳定。同源性分析表明，生成的序列并非已知蛋白的全长拷贝，而是将匹配天然蛋白的短片段与新颖的模型生成序列相结合。基于描述符的筛选对短生成序列进行，产生了一个无序候选池，从中选出五个合成可行的肽段用于实验测试。其中四个在近生理条件下显示出凝聚样特征，包括液滴状组装和浊度增加。对较长生成序列子集进行的粗粒化相共存模拟显示广泛的相分离倾向，其中89条序列中有12条与强相分离的hnRNPA1低复杂度域相当。这些结果表明，紧凑的任务特异性生成模型可以从小型精选数据集中学习信息丰富的序列语法，并提出可实验测试的凝聚形成肽段。
